facts.text: In simulation, a material describes how a surface responds to light, radio waves or sound; ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D is a standard format for storing those properties for camera, lidar and radar.
facts.quote: In simulation, a material is the description of how a surface responds to light, radio waves or sound, and ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D is a standard format for storing those properties for camera, lidar and radar.

facts.text: Simulator materials must specify sensor-specific properties: lidar reflectance at the laser wavelength and each angle; radar permittivity, conductivity and roughness; camera color, roughness and shininess; and ultrasonic sound absorption and scattering.
facts.quote: for lidar, its reflectance at the laser's wavelength and at each angle; for radar, its electrical properties (permittivity and conductivity) and roughness; for a camera, its color, roughness and shininess; for ultrasonic sensors, how it absorbs and scatters sound

facts.text: The booklet finds that a material's non-visual response cannot be derived from a visual texture.
facts.quote: The booklet's key finding is that non-visual response cannot be derived from a visual texture.

facts.text: The standards association ASAM released ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D version 1.0.0 on 3 April 2025.
facts.quote: ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D version 1.0.0, released 3 April 2025 by the standards association ASAM

facts.text: ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D version 1.0.0 stores wavelength-dependent lookup tables for lidar, radar and camera properties, with license information per material.
facts.quote: stores wavelength-dependent lookup tables for lidar, radar and camera properties, with license information per material

facts.text: Weather, lighting and dirt on the sensor housing are outside the scope of ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D version 1.0.0.
facts.quote: weather, lighting and dirt on the sensor housing are outside its scope

facts.text: ASAM OpenMATERIAL 3D version 1.1.0 was planned for October 2026.
facts.quote: a version 1.1.0 was planned for October 2026

facts.text: Different lidar wavelengths need separate material definitions.
facts.quote: Different lidar wavelengths need separate definitions.

facts.text: A ray-traced radar simulation using standard material values produced about 12% of the real point density: 251 versus 2,057 points per frame. The passage attributes the discrepancy to real radar's diffuse scattering and multiple bounces.
facts.quote: a ray-traced radar simulation using standard material values produced about 12% of the real point density (251 against 2,057 points per frame), because real radar includes diffuse scattering and multiple bounces

facts.text: No published material datasets were found for job-site materials—rock, wet clay, gravel, steel buckets and high-visibility clothing—at lidar wavelengths or radar bands.
facts.quote: No published material datasets for job-site materials (rock, wet clay, gravel, steel buckets, high-visibility clothing) at lidar wavelengths or radar bands were found

facts.text: No published ultrasonic or thermal material datasets were found.

facts.text: The material layer required by both standards and vendors does not exist for mines and quarries, so the collision mitigation validation program would have to measure the material properties itself.

facts.text: Sensor simulation of dust, wet rock and metal clutter remains unvalidated until the collision mitigation validation program measures the missing mine and quarry material properties.
